record.paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
record.original_question: Construct small-amplitude time-quasiperiodic solutions of the massless φ^4 equation u_tt=u_xx−u^3 on the one-dimensional torus.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.3.4 (S. Kuksin) Construct small amplitude time quasiperiodic solutions for the massless r.p4 equation Utt = U xx - u3 , x E Tl.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the massless φ⁴ nonlinear wave equation
   u_tt = u_xx − u³,   x ∈ T¹ = R/2πZ,   t ∈ R,
posed on the one-dimensional torus with periodic boundary conditions. Note that this equation is completely resonant: the linearized equation u_tt = u_xx has the integer spectrum of frequencies {|k| : k ∈ Z}, so there is no parameter (such as a mass term m²u or a potential V(x)u) to tune frequencies away from resonances.

Problem. For any integer d ≥ 2, construct small-amplitude time-quasiperiodic solutions of this equation with d rationally independent frequencies. More precisely, exhibit a positive-measure (in the sense of Lebesgue or Whitney-smooth Cantor-like) family of frequency vectors ω = (ω₁,…,ω_d) ∈ R^d and corresponding classical (or analytic) solutions
   u(t,x) = U(ω₁ t, …, ω_d t, x),
where U : T^d × T¹ → R is continuous (and as smooth as possible), such that ‖u‖ → 0 as the family parameter tends to zero, and such that the closure of the orbit {(ω₁ t, …, ω_d t) : t ∈ R} is dense in T^d.
artifact.category_tag: KAM theory for completely resonant wave equations
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: quasi-periodic solutions with two frequencies for completely resonant nonlinear wave equations u_tt − u_xx ± u³ = 0 on T¹ have been constructed (Berti–Bolle, Gentile–Procesi, and related works), typically via Lyapunov–Schmidt reduction combined with resummation/Nash–Moser techniques. The general case of arbitrarily many frequencies for the massless φ⁴ equation on T¹ does not appear to be fully resolved in the literature, so the problem in its full generality is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-periodic solutions for completely resonant non-linear wave equations in 1D and 2D
status_evidence.snippet: Quasi-periodic solutions with two frequencies are provided for a class of completely resonant nonlinear wave equations in one and two spatial dimensions with periodic boundary conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Two-frequency quasi-periodic solutions have been constructed for completely resonant 1D and 2D nonlinear wave equations including the cubic case.

status_evidence.title: Periodic Solutions for Completely Resonant Nonlinear Wave Equations with Dirichlet Boundary Conditions
status_evidence.snippet: Small amplitude periodic solutions of u_tt − u_xx + u³ = 0 are constructed for a large Lebesgue measure set of frequencies near 1.
status_evidence.claim: Periodic (single-frequency) solutions to the cubic resonant wave equation are known.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-Periodic Solutions of Completely Resonant Forced Wave Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of quasi-periodic solutions with two frequencies of completely resonant, periodically forced nonlinear wave equations with periodic spatial boundary conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial progress on quasi-periodic solutions in the completely resonant setting.
